## Design brief excerpt: Ashgrove Kitchen & Pantry
Client: private residence, Ashgrove neighborhood. Scope: full kitchen and adjoining pantry renovation,
including new cabinetry, countertops, backsplash tile, lighting, and hardware. The client wants a warm,
grounded palette built around the moss green and warm sand tones already used in the living room, extended
into the kitchen without making the two spaces feel identical. Cabinetry should read as furniture rather than
built-in boxes: shaker doors, a mix of open shelving and closed storage, and a single statement piece (the
pantry hutch) that can stand alone if the kitchen is ever reconfigured. Countertops need to handle a household
that cooks daily, so durability comes before pure looks, though the client has been clear they don't want
anything that reads as "commercial kitchen."


## Material spec sheet: Moss Green Ceramic backsplash tile
Manufacturer: Fenwick Tileworks. Size: 3 x 6 inch subway format, gloss finish. Coverage needed: 42 square
feet including 10% waste allowance for cuts around outlets and the window trim. Grout: warm gray, unsanded,
1/16 inch joints. Lead time from order to delivery is currently quoted at 5 to 7 weeks, which needs to be
confirmed against the install schedule before we lock the date with the tile setter. This tile has been used
on two prior Birchcroft projects and held up well in both; no known issues with the glaze under normal kitchen
use, including near the range.


## Material spec sheet: Warm Sand Quartz countertop
Manufacturer: Latigo Stone. Slab size: 126 x 63 inches, enough for the full run including the island in a
single slab with no visible seam except at the island's back corner, which is unavoidable given the layout.
Edge profile: eased edge, 1.25 inch thickness. Sealant: none required, quartz is non-porous. Client asked
about a waterfall edge on the island; this would need an additional slab and adds meaningfully to cost, noted
as an open decision pending the revised budget conversation.


## Site visit notes, June 15
Walked the site with the general contractor this morning. Framing for the pantry nook is complete and matches
the plan within a half inch, no adjustments needed. Electrical rough-in for the under-cabinet lighting is
scheduled for next week. Flagged one issue: the window trim on the north wall is slightly out of square,
which will affect how the backsplash tile terminates at that corner, we'll need a scribe piece cut on site
rather than relying on a factory edge. Took photos of the rough plumbing location for the pantry sink to
confirm it lines up with the fixture cut sheet before the counter template appointment.


## Meeting notes: weekly client check-in
Attendees: client, lead designer, project coordinator. Reviewed the latest site photos together on the
portal, client liked seeing the progress photos sorted by date rather than having to guess which was newest.
Discussed the punch list: two items closed since last week (touch-up paint in the hallway, adjusted cabinet
door alignment on the pantry hutch), three remain open pending the electrician's return visit. Client asked
whether the material swatches shown in the portal reflect final selections or are still open for change; we
confirmed everything except hardware finish is locked, hardware is still open pending one more sample.


## QA notes from the build team
Went through the client portal on a phone and a tablet before this week's check-in to catch anything before
the client does. On the phone, the material grid felt tight with three columns once the price tag moved
below the name, worth flagging to the person who owns the layout. The floor plan zoom control in the corner
is easy to miss on a small screen, might be worth a label or a slightly larger tap target later. Everything
else read fine: photo captions, punch list, and the project header all held up at narrow widths.


## Changelog, internal
May 22: Added site photo capture-date sorting to the portal template, previously sorted by upload time only.
May 30: Fixed a spacing issue in the material swatch grid header row on tablet widths.
June 3: Added the punch-list open-item count to the section heading across all portal templates, not just
this project's.
June 9: Corrected a typo in the shared empty-state copy ("Swatchs" to "Swatches") across every project using
the default Studio Layer template; individual project overrides were not touched by that change.


## Vendor correspondence summary: hardware finish
Reached out to two hardware vendors for the pantry hutch pulls. Vendor A quotes brushed brass at $18 per pull,
four week lead time, minimum order of twelve. Vendor B offers a similar brushed brass finish at $22 per pull
but can turn around in two weeks, which matters if the install date holds. Neither vendor's brushed brass
photographs quite match the swatch sample the client approved in person, worth requesting a physical sample
from each before ordering rather than relying on product photos alone.


## Punch list detail, carried from last walkthrough
Open: adjust the pantry hutch door alignment on the lower left cabinet, it currently sits about 2mm proud of
its neighbor. Open: recheck the backsplash tile grout color once the north wall scribe piece is installed,
compare against the rest of the run in daylight. Open: confirm under-cabinet lighting color temperature
against the pendant fixtures over the island, client mentioned the sample felt slightly cooler than expected.
Closed: touch-up paint in the hallway leading to the pantry. Closed: cabinet door alignment on the island run.

content.text: Okay, before I hand this back for the final look, I want to do one more sweep of the actual copy on the page rather than just the layout pieces I've been touching all afternoon. Priya's been giving layout and behavior feedback all session, but nobody has looked closely at the words themselves: headings, button labels, the material descriptions pulled from the catalog, the punch-list section title, the empty states. Given she just said she wants to ship this and send the client the link, a typo in the hero heading or a leftover 'lorem ipsum' in a material description would be a worse look than any of the layout issues we've already fixed. Rather than hand-picking a few spots, it makes more sense to hand the whole current page content to the content tool with one broad instruction covering casing, stray punctuation, and inconsistent terminology (we've called it both 'material swatch' and 'material sample' in different spots, and it should just be one term). That's going to turn up more matches than a targeted edit would, and I should expect some of them to be ambiguous, places where a word looks off but changing it needs a judgment call the tool can't safely make on its own, like a client-supplied room name that happens to look like a typo. I'll let it apply the ones it's confident about and leave the rest flagged so I can call them out by hand in the summary instead of guessing.

## Design brief excerpt: Ashgrove Kitchen & Pantry
Client: private residence, Ashgrove neighborhood. Scope: full kitchen and adjoining pantry renovation,
including new cabinetry, countertops, backsplash tile, lighting, and hardware. The client wants a warm,
grounded palette built around the moss green and warm sand tones already used in the living room, extended
into the kitchen without making the two spaces feel identical. Cabinetry should read as furniture rather than
built-in boxes: shaker doors, a mix of open shelving and closed storage, and a single statement piece (the
pantry hutch) that can stand alone if the kitchen is ever reconfigured. Countertops need to handle a household
that cooks daily, so durability comes before pure looks, though the client has been clear they don't want
anything that reads as "commercial kitchen."


## Material spec sheet: Moss Green Ceramic backsplash tile
Manufacturer: Fenwick Tileworks. Size: 3 x 6 inch subway format, gloss finish. Coverage needed: 42 square
feet including 10% waste allowance for cuts around outlets and the window trim. Grout: warm gray, unsanded,
1/16 inch joints. Lead time from order to delivery is currently quoted at 5 to 7 weeks, which needs to be
confirmed against the install schedule before we lock the date with the tile setter. This tile has been used
on two prior Birchcroft projects and held up well in both; no known issues with the glaze under normal kitchen
use, including near the range.


## Material spec sheet: Warm Sand Quartz countertop
Manufacturer: Latigo Stone. Slab size: 126 x 63 inches, enough for the full run including the island in a
single slab with no visible seam except at the island's back corner, which is unavoidable given the layout.
Edge profile: eased edge, 1.25 inch thickness. Sealant: none required, quartz is non-porous. Client asked
about a waterfall edge on the island; this would need an additional slab and adds meaningfully to cost, noted
as an open decision pending the revised budget conversation.


## Site visit notes, June 15
Walked the site with the general contractor this morning. Framing for the pantry nook is complete and matches
the plan within a half inch, no adjustments needed. Electrical rough-in for the under-cabinet lighting is
scheduled for next week. Flagged one issue: the window trim on the north wall is slightly out of square,
which will affect how the backsplash tile terminates at that corner, we'll need a scribe piece cut on site
rather than relying on a factory edge. Took photos of the rough plumbing location for the pantry sink to
confirm it lines up with the fixture cut sheet before the counter template appointment.


## Meeting notes: weekly client check-in
Attendees: client, lead designer, project coordinator. Reviewed the latest site photos together on the
portal, client liked seeing the progress photos sorted by date rather than having to guess which was newest.
Discussed the punch list: two items closed since last week (touch-up paint in the hallway, adjusted cabinet
door alignment on the pantry hutch), three remain open pending the electrician's return visit. Client asked
whether the material swatches shown in the portal reflect final selections or are still open for change; we
confirmed everything except hardware finish is locked, hardware is still open pending one more sample.


## QA notes from the build team
Went through the client portal on a phone and a tablet before this week's check-in to catch anything before
the client does. On the phone, the material grid felt tight with three columns once the price tag moved
below the name, worth flagging to the person who owns the layout. The floor plan zoom control in the corner
is easy to miss on a small screen, might be worth a label or a slightly larger tap target later. Everything
else read fine: photo captions, punch list, and the project header all held up at narrow widths.


## Changelog, internal
May 22: Added site photo capture-date sorting to the portal template, previously sorted by upload time only.
May 30: Fixed a spacing issue in the material swatch grid header row on tablet widths.
June 3: Added the punch-list open-item count to the section heading across all portal templates, not just
this project's.
June 9: Corrected a typo in the shared empty-state copy ("Swatchs" to "Swatches") across every project using
the default Studio Layer template; individual project overrides were not touched by that change.


## Vendor correspondence summary: hardware finish
Reached out to two hardware vendors for the pantry hutch pulls. Vendor A quotes brushed brass at $18 per pull,
four week lead time, minimum order of twelve. Vendor B offers a similar brushed brass finish at $22 per pull
but can turn around in two weeks, which matters if the install date holds. Neither vendor's brushed brass
photographs quite match the swatch sample the client approved in person, worth requesting a physical sample
from each before ordering rather than relying on product photos alone.


## Punch list detail, carried from last walkthrough
Open: adjust the pantry hutch door alignment on the lower left cabinet, it currently sits about 2mm proud of
its neighbor. Open: recheck the backsplash tile grout color once the north wall scribe piece is installed,
compare against the rest of the run in daylight. Open: confirm under-cabinet lighting color temperature
against the pendant fixtures over the island, client mentioned the sample felt slightly cooler than expected.
Closed: touch-up paint in the hallway leading to the pantry. Closed: cabinet door alignment on the island run.
